lastCompletedStory.title: Promote the CAM-382 false-positive cases into the executed matrix and extend the fixture-shape guard

nextStoryContext: oracle-lint-cases.txt grew from 17 to 26 live rows: 9 new frozen-comparand rows were promoted from the INNER strings embedded in test/fixtures/oracle-lint/cam382-false-positives.txt's bun -e/grep -qF wrapper commands (the wrapper commands themselves were already rows, added by US-001/US-002; their -e payload is not scanned by the rule so the wrapper form alone never exercised the rule against the inner strings). Ground truth for each new row was derived by running the real rule directly (bun -e import of src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts), not by trusting the fixture file's own 'false-positives' name or the PRD notes' 'verdict ok' generalization: the four-operator set (`test $X -eq 41` etc., plus the mainbranch grep-pattern line) is actually a MISSED-detection/false-negative guard and correctly classifies as flag, while `cmd --ge 5` / `echo foo-eq 42` / `run --eq 7` / `test $(foo-eq 42)` are the genuine false-positive guards and classify as ok (see patterns.md, new bullet before the US-002 CAM-382 entry). cam382-false-positives.txt is retained as historical documentation (header comment updated) since none of its content is now the ONLY executed home of a case. test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts gained a shared parseFixtureRows() helper (the pre-existing 'every row classifies' test was refactored to use it, no behavior change) and a new 'oracle-lint-cases.txt fixture-shape guard' describe block: assertFixtureShape() now asserts rows.length>0 AND at least one double-quoted interpreter-wrapper row (bash/sh/zsh/dash -c "...") AND at least one backslash-escape row exist, plus a mutation-sweep test that strips every double-quoted-wrapper row from a temp copy (mkdtempSync) and expects assertFixtureShape to throw, printing the stripped count first. RULES still has exactly 4 named rules; no src/ changes this story (fixture + test only).
